title: Chvátal's conjecture and sharp Boolean correlation
abstract: Formalizes Chang, Liu, and Liu's proof that a hereditary family on a finite nonempty ground set has a largest intersecting subfamily that is a star. Develops the sharp Boolean Fourier correlation inequality, its antipodal and quadratic forms, sharpness examples, and the weighted star theorem for nonnegative decreasing weights.

informal.Chvatal.chvatal: Every intersecting subfamily A of a hereditary finite family D on a finite nonempty ground type has cardinality at most that of some star of D.
informal.Chvatal.exists_largest_intersecting_star: One star of D is itself intersecting and simultaneously dominates all intersecting subfamilies of the hereditary family D in size, on a finite nonempty ground type.
informal.Chvatal.sharp_correlation: For increasing Boolean functions f and g on any finite cube, the sum of squared Fourier coefficients of g weighted by the largest influence of f on each nonempty index is at most the harmonic mean of Cov(f,g) and Cov(f,g*), with zero-denominator value zero.
informal.Chvatal.two_spectral_le_quadratic_covari: For increasing Boolean f and g and every real t, twice their squared Fourier energy over index pairs with odd intersection is bounded by t^2 Cov(f,g) + (1-t)^2 Cov(f,g*).
informal.Chvatal.antipodal_correlation: If g is also self-dual and the finite coordinate type is nonempty, Cov(f,g) is at least one quarter of f's minimum coordinate influence.
informal.Chvatal.andFunction_sharp: The AND function attains equality in the sharp correlation bound for every increasing Boolean second function, including constants.
informal.Chvatal.exists_largest_weighted_intersec: For any nonnegative antitone real weight on subsets of a finite nonempty ground type, one full-cube star is intersecting and its total weight dominates every intersecting family.
